name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
description: The assisted pull-up machine uses a counter-weighted platform that the exerciser kneels or stands on, reducing the effective bodyweight being lifted. It allows beginners or those building toward an unassisted pull-up to train the full pulling movement pattern with correct form. The machine's assistance decreases as strength improves, providing a progressive path toward bodyweight pull-ups.

execution.starting_position: Set the desired assistance weight on the machine. Kneel or stand on the counter-weighted platform. Grip the overhead handles at shoulder width with an overhand grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Select a heavier assistance weight to make the exercise easier (more weight counter-balances more of your body weight). Adjust the platform height.
steps: Step 1: Kneel on the platform and grip the handles with an overhand shoulder-width grip.
Step 2: Begin with arms fully extended and scapulae elevated.
Step 3: Depress the scapulae and initiate the pull by driving the elbows toward the floor.
Step 4: Continue pulling until the chin clears the handles or chest approaches the bar.
Step 5: Lower under full control until arms are extended and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
common_mistakes: Using too much assistance weight, reducing training stimulus
Letting the platform crash down uncontrolled on each rep
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
safety_considerations: Step off the platform carefully when dismounting — the platform will drop if you step off while weight is selected
Progressively reduce assistance over time to build toward unassisted pull-ups
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom, chin above handle level at the top.
coaching_cues: Think about putting your shoulder blades in your back pockets
Full extension at the bottom every rep
